checks.label: Security Patch Level
checks.command: PATCH_DATE=$(getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$PATCH_DATE" ]; then echo 'UNKNOWN'; exit 1; fi; PATCH_EPOCH=$(date -d "$PATCH_DATE" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0); CURRENT_EPOCH=$(date +%s); DAYS_OLD=$(( ($CURRENT_EPOCH - $PATCH_EPOCH) / 86400 )); if [ $DAYS_OLD -lt 90 ]; then echo "RECENT: $PATCH_DATE ($DAYS_OLD days old)"; else echo "OUTDATED: $PATCH_DATE ($DAYS_OLD days old)"; fi
checks.description: Security patch must be less than 90 days old
checks.remediation: Apply the latest OTA security update or flash an updated system image with a patch level less than 90 days old.

checks.label: Third-Party App Stores
checks.description: Avoid non-Google app stores
checks.remediation: Uninstall third-party app stores. Run: pm uninstall <package_name> for each detected store.

checks.label: User-installed Apps
checks.description: Check how many user apps installed
checks.remediation: Review the list with pm list packages -3 and uninstall unnecessary apps: pm uninstall <package_name>.

checks.label: Unusual Files in /sdcard/
checks.description: Sensitive files in user-accessible storage
checks.remediation: Remove sensitive files from /sdcard/. Run: adb shell rm /sdcard/<filename> for each flagged file.

checks.label: Wi-Fi SSID
checks.description: Shows current Wi-Fi network
checks.remediation: Informational only. Verify the device is connected to an authorized network.

checks.label: Zygote Process Check
checks.description: Zygote process is core to Android app lifecycle
checks.remediation: If zygote is missing, the system is severely compromised. Reflash the factory firmware image immediately.

checks.label: Wi-Fi Direct Disabled (WFD)
checks.description: Wi-Fi Direct (WFD) package should be removed if unused
checks.remediation: Disable or uninstall the WFD package. Run: pm disable <wfd_package> or pm uninstall <wfd_package>.

checks.label: Auto System Update Enabled
checks.description: Auto updates improve patch consistency
checks.remediation: Enable auto updates. Run: adb shell settings put global auto_update_system 1.

checks.label: Credential Storage Contents
checks.description: Number of credential files in keystore user_0 - informational evidence collector.
checks.remediation: Review keystore contents if unexpectedly large. Run: adb shell ls /data/misc/keystore/user_0 (requires root).

checks.label: Kernel Hardening (PAN/UAO)
checks.description: Privileged Access Never (PAN) and User Access Override (UAO) should be enabled for memory protection
checks.remediation: Rebuild the kernel with CONFIG_ARM64_PAN=y and CONFIG_ARM64_UAO=y in the defconfig, then reflash.

checks.label: World-Writable Directories
checks.description: World-writable directories in system
checks.remediation: Remove world-write permission. Run: chmod o-w <directory> for each flagged path (requires root/remount).

checks.label: SUID Binaries
checks.description: SUID binaries - review for privilege escalation
checks.remediation: Review each SUID binary. Remove the SUID bit from unnecessary ones: chmod u-s <binary> (requires remount).

checks.label: Exposed Unix Sockets
checks.description: Unix sockets - potential IPC attack vectors
checks.remediation: Review each socket owner and permissions. Restrict access with chmod 600 on sockets not needed by other users.

checks.label: Debugfs Mounted
checks.description: Debugfs mounted - kernel debug info exposed
checks.remediation: Unmount debugfs. Run: umount /sys/kernel/debug. Prevent at boot by removing debugfs from fstab.

checks.label: Executable Stack
checks.description: ASLR should be enabled
checks.remediation: Enable ASLR. Run: echo 2 > /proc/sys/kernel/randomize_va_space. Persist via sysctl.conf.

checks.label: Ptrace Scope
checks.description: Ptrace restrictions (1+ recommended)
checks.remediation: Restrict ptrace. Run: echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope. Persist via sysctl.conf.

checks.label: Recent Kernel Crashes
checks.description: Recent kernel panics or fatal errors
checks.remediation: Investigate crash logs for root cause. Update the kernel or drivers if a known bug is identified.

checks.label: Application Crash Log
checks.description: Recent app crash logs (look for repeated exceptions)
checks.remediation: Review crash logs with: adb logcat -b crash. Update or reinstall repeatedly crashing applications.

checks.label: Stack Canaries
checks.description: Stack canaries should be enabled to prevent buffer overflows
checks.remediation: Rebuild the kernel with CONFIG_CC_STACKPROTECTOR_STRONG=y in the defconfig, then reflash.

checks.label: ROP Mitigation (PAC)
checks.description: Pointer Authentication (PAC) should be enabled to prevent ROP attacks
checks.remediation: Rebuild the kernel with CONFIG_ARM64_PTR_AUTH=y in the defconfig. Requires ARMv8.3+ hardware.

checks.label: Memory Tagging (MTE)
checks.description: Memory Tagging Extension (MTE) should be enabled for JIT hardening
checks.remediation: Rebuild the kernel with CONFIG_ARM64_MTE=y in the defconfig. Requires ARMv8.5+ hardware.

checks.label: Processes Running as Root
checks.description: Minimize processes running as root
checks.remediation: Identify unnecessary root processes and reconfigure their init.rc entries to run under a dedicated UID.

checks.label: World-Readable Proc Entries
checks.description: Process info readable - normal but review sensitive processes
checks.remediation: Set hidepid=2 on /proc mount to restrict process visibility. Add hidepid=2 to fstab for /proc.

checks.label: Custom Native Daemons
checks.command: ps -A 2>/dev/null | grep -vE 'zygote|system_server|surfaceflinger|android|google|com\.|app_process|dalvikvm' | grep -E '^root|^system' | awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq | head -10
checks.description: Non-Android native processes - review for IoT services
checks.remediation: Review each custom daemon. Remove or disable unneeded ones by editing their init.rc service entries.

checks.label: Listening on All Interfaces
checks.command: netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep '0.0.0.0:' | grep -v '127.0.0.1' || ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep '0.0.0.0:' | head -10
checks.description: Services listening on all interfaces - exposed to network
checks.remediation: Bind services to 127.0.0.1 instead of 0.0.0.0, or use iptables to restrict access to trusted IPs only.

checks.label: Stack Protection Status
checks.description: Stack protection status
checks.remediation: Informational. If stack protection is missing, rebuild binaries with -fstack-protector-strong.

checks.label: Writable Paths in $PATH
checks.command: echo $PATH | tr ':' '\n' | while IFS= read -r d; do [ -n "$d" ] && [ -w "$d" ] && echo "$d"; done
checks.description: Writable dirs in PATH can lead to privilege escalation
checks.remediation: Remove write permissions on PATH directories. Run: chmod o-w <dir> and chmod g-w <dir> for each flagged path.

checks.label: Disable-Verity Property Not Set
checks.description: Disable-verity must not be enabled on locked devices
checks.remediation: Re-enable verity. Run: adb enable-verity, then reboot. Remove persist.sys.disable_verity from build.prop.

checks.label: Battery Saver Mode
checks.description: Battery saver status
checks.remediation: Informational. Toggle battery saver via: adb shell settings put global low_power 0 (or 1 to enable).

checks.label: Doze Mode Enabled
checks.description: Doze mode for battery optimization
checks.remediation: Informational. Enable doze if disabled via: adb shell dumpsys deviceidle enable.

checks.label: Doze Whitelist Apps
checks.description: Apps excluded from doze mode
checks.remediation: Review whitelist and remove unnecessary apps. Run: adb shell dumpsys deviceidle whitelist -<package>.

checks.label: Top 5 Running Processes
checks.description: Initial list of active processes
checks.remediation: Informational. Review the process list for unexpected or unknown entries.

checks.label: bootctl Present
checks.command: command -v bootctl >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo present || echo absent
checks.description: bootctl available to query slot state
checks.remediation: Informational. If absent, A/B slot management is unavailable - verify the device supports A/B updates.

checks.label: Current Slot
checks.description: Device reports current boot slot (a/b or 0/1)
checks.remediation: Informational. If the slot is unexpected, check for failed OTA updates with: bootctl get-suffix.

checks.label: Stock Recovery (No TWRP in PATH)
checks.command: command -v twrp >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo found || echo notfound
checks.description: No custom recovery binary should be present
checks.remediation: Remove the TWRP binary and reflash stock recovery. Run: rm $(which twrp) and flash stock recovery image.

checks.label: Kernel Version
checks.description: Kernel build/version details
checks.remediation: Informational. Record the kernel version and verify it matches the expected vendor release.

checks.label: Audit Logs Enabled
checks.description: Kernel printk log levels (evidence collector)
checks.remediation: Informational. Ensure adequate log levels are set. Adjust with: echo '7 4 1 7' > /proc/sys/kernel/printk.

checks.label: KASLR Enabled
checks.description: Kernel Address Space Layout Randomization (KASLR) should be enabled to randomize kernel memory layout.
checks.remediation: Enable KASLR by adding 'kaslr' to the kernel command line in the bootloader config, then reboot.

checks.label: NX (No eXecute) Bit Enabled
checks.description: NX bit must be enabled to prevent execution of code in data memory regions.
checks.remediation: Ensure NX/XD is enabled in BIOS/UEFI settings. Rebuild the kernel with PAE support if NX is missing.

checks.label: Core Dumps Disabled
checks.description: Core dumps should be disabled to prevent sensitive data leakage.
checks.remediation: Disable core dumps. Run: echo '|/dev/null' > /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern. Persist via sysctl.conf.

checks.label: SECCOMP Enabled
checks.description: SECCOMP must be enabled to restrict system calls.
checks.remediation: Rebuild the kernel with CONFIG_SECCOMP=y in the defconfig, then reflash the device.

checks.label: Protected Symlinks Enabled
checks.description: Symlink protection should be enabled to prevent symlink-based privilege escalation.
checks.remediation: Run: echo 1 > /proc/sys/fs/protected_symlinks. Persist by adding fs.protected_symlinks=1 to sysctl.conf.

checks.label: Protected Hardlinks Enabled
checks.description: Hardlink protection should be enabled to prevent unauthorized file access.
checks.remediation: Run: echo 1 > /proc/sys/fs/protected_hardlinks. Persist by adding fs.protected_hardlinks=1 to sysctl.conf.

checks.label: Debug Build Type
checks.description: Must be 'user' build. 'userdebug' or 'eng' allow debugging
checks.remediation: Set ro.build.type=user in build.prop and rebuild the system image. Do not ship userdebug or eng builds.

checks.label: Debuggable Flag
checks.description: ro.debuggable=1 allows ptrace, debugging - must be 0
checks.remediation: Set ro.debuggable=0 in build.prop and rebuild the system image.

checks.label: ADB Secure Mode
checks.description: ro.adb.secure=1 requires RSA authentication for ADB
checks.remediation: Set ro.adb.secure=1 in build.prop and rebuild the system image to enforce ADB RSA authentication.

checks.label: ADB Root Access
checks.description: ADB shell should NOT run as root (uid=0)
checks.remediation: Use a user build (ro.build.type=user) which drops ADB to shell user. Run: adb unroot to demote.

checks.label: dm-verity Mode
checks.description: dm-verity must fail closed to protect system partitions. Secure modes are 'enforcing', 'eio' (AVB-recommended managed mode), 'restart' and 'panicking'. 'ignore_corruption'/'logging' may return corrupt data and 'disabled' means no verity.
checks.remediation: Run: adb enable-verity and reboot. Ensure ro.boot.veritymode is enforcing or eio (managed). Avoid ignore_corruption/logging/disabled.

checks.label: Default Build Fingerprint
checks.description: Generic/test build fingerprint indicates development firmware
checks.remediation: Rebuild with a proper production fingerprint. Set ro.build.fingerprint to the official release value.

checks.label: Manufacturer Default Unchanged
checks.description: Device model indicates test/development unit
checks.remediation: Flash production firmware. Set ro.product.model to the correct model name in build.prop.

checks.label: Debug Properties Set
checks.description: Debug properties enabled - may leak sensitive info
checks.remediation: Remove debug properties from build.prop. Run: adb shell setprop <debug.property> '' for runtime removal.

checks.label: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
checks.description: Total packages - FDA requires SBOM for premarket submissions
checks.remediation: Informational. Export the full package list with: pm list packages -f > sbom_packages.txt for SBOM tracking.

checks.label: Third-Party Libraries
checks.description: Shared libraries count - document for SBOM/vulnerability tracking
checks.remediation: Informational. Catalog shared libraries for vulnerability scanning and SBOM documentation.

checks.label: Build Timestamp
checks.description: Firmware build date - document for configuration management
checks.remediation: Informational. Record the build date for audit trails and configuration management.

checks.label: TEE Driver Presence (Present → Info)
checks.description: TEE device nodes found (e.g., /dev/tee*, /dev/trusty*). Presence is informational.
checks.remediation: Informational. Verify TEE is functional by checking keymaster/gatekeeper HAL status.

checks.label: TEE Vendor Prop (Empty → Verify)
checks.description: Empty output is common (vendors often hide TEE props); flag for manual verify.
checks.remediation: Manually verify TEE functionality by testing hardware-backed keystore operations.

checks.label: TPM Keystore Presence
checks.description: Checks for hardware-backed keystore modules
checks.remediation: Ensure a hardware-backed keystore HAL is present. Install the vendor-specific keystore module if missing.

checks.label: Auto Time Enabled
checks.description: Auto time sync helps prevent cert/token attacks
checks.remediation: Enable auto time sync. Run: adb shell settings put global auto_time 1.

checks.label: Auto Timezone
checks.description: Automatic timezone detection
checks.remediation: Enable auto timezone. Run: adb shell settings put global auto_time_zone 1.

checks.label: NTP Server
checks.description: Configured NTP server for time sync
checks.remediation: Set a trusted NTP server. Run: adb shell settings put global ntp_server time.google.com.

checks.label: Time Zone
checks.description: Current timezone setting
checks.remediation: Set the correct timezone. Run: adb shell setprop persist.sys.timezone <Region/City>.

checks.label: WebView Provider
checks.description: WebView implementation provider
checks.remediation: Set an official WebView provider. Run: adb shell settings put global webview_provider com.google.android.webview.

checks.label: WebView Version
checks.command: dumpsys package com.google.android.webview 2>/dev/null | grep versionName | head -1
checks.description: WebView version - should be updated
checks.remediation: Update WebView via Play Store or sideload the latest APK: pm install -r <webview.apk>.

checks.label: Safe Boot Disallowed
checks.description: safe_boot_disallowed controls whether the device may be rebooted into Safe Boot. Note: this is unrelated to WebView SafeBrowsing (see separate check). Informational; the value indicates whether OEM or admin policy restricts Safe Boot access.
checks.remediation: Informational. Review safe boot policy settings in your device management configuration.

checks.label: Emulator Detection (QEMU)
checks.description: QEMU emulator property set - POS and IoT devices must run on physical hardware, not emulators
checks.remediation: Deploy on physical hardware only. If testing, remove ro.kernel.qemu property from build.prop.

checks.label: Virtual Hardware Detection
checks.description: Virtual/emulated hardware detected - goldfish/ranchu=Android emulator, vbox=VirtualBox
checks.remediation: Deploy on physical hardware. Virtual environments are not suitable for production POS/IoT devices.

checks.label: System Memory Status
checks.description: System memory baseline - abnormally low available memory may indicate memory scraping attacks or crypto mining
checks.remediation: Informational. Investigate if available memory is abnormally low - check for rogue processes with top or ps.

checks.label: Suspicious Executables in /data/local/tmp
checks.description: Executable files in /data/local/tmp - common staging location for exploits, Frida gadgets, and malware payloads
checks.remediation: Remove all executables. Run: adb shell rm /data/local/tmp/<filename> for each flagged file.

checks.label: SIM Card / Cellular Status
checks.description: SIM card state - POS terminals and IoT kiosks typically should not have active cellular connectivity
checks.remediation: If cellular is not required, disable the radio. Run: adb shell settings put global airplane_mode_on 1.

checks.label: High CPU Usage Processes
checks.description: Processes using >50% CPU - may indicate crypto miners or RAM scrapers
checks.remediation: Identify and kill suspicious high-CPU processes. Run: kill <pid>. Investigate and remove the binary.

checks.label: System Packages Total Count
checks.description: Total system package count (typical: 80-250) - compare against device baseline for tampering
checks.remediation: Compare count against a known-good baseline. Investigate discrepancies with: pm list packages -s.

checks.label: Process Memory Maps Count
checks.description: Running process count via maps - baseline for anomaly detection (typical: 50-200)
checks.remediation: Compare against a known baseline. If count is abnormally high, investigate unknown processes with ps -A.

checks.label: SECCOMP-BPF Kernel Support
checks.description: SECCOMP-BPF (Secure Computing with Berkeley Packet Filter) restricts syscall access per-process. Required for Android app sandbox hardening. Missing CONFIG_SECCOMP_FILTER is a kernel hardening gap.
checks.remediation: Ensure kernel is compiled with CONFIG_SECCOMP=y and CONFIG_SECCOMP_FILTER=y. Required for Android app process sandboxing.

checks.label: SECCOMP Status of Init (PID 1)
checks.description: SECCOMP mode of init process: 0=disabled, 1=strict, 2=filter (BPF). Mode 2 indicates SECCOMP-BPF syscall filtering is active.
checks.remediation: Informational. SECCOMP mode 2 (filter) is expected on hardened Android systems.

checks.label: SECCOMP Status of Zygote
checks.command: pid=$(pidof zygote 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}'); [ -n "$pid" ] && cat /proc/$pid/status 2>/dev/null | grep Seccomp || echo 'zygote_not_found'
checks.description: Zygote is the parent of all Android app processes. SECCOMP filter mode 2 on Zygote ensures all spawned apps inherit syscall filtering.
checks.remediation: SECCOMP mode 2 on Zygote is required for Android app sandbox. Verify seccomp_bpf is enabled in Android init.

checks.label: Qualcomm QSEE TEE Device Node
checks.description: Qualcomm Secure Execution Environment (QSEE) device node. Presence confirms Qualcomm TrustZone TEE is active on this device.
checks.remediation: Informational. QSEE is the Qualcomm TEE implementation. Ensure QSEE is running and not exploitable via CVE-2015-6639 / CVE-2016-2431.

checks.label: Qualcomm TEE (QTEE) Properties
checks.description: Qualcomm TEE (QTEE/QSEE) system properties. Indicates Qualcomm TrustZone-based security services are active.
checks.remediation: Informational. Verify Qualcomm security patches are applied for TEE-related CVEs.

checks.label: MediaTek Mobicore TEE Device Node
checks.description: MediaTek Mobicore (t-base) TEE device nodes. Presence confirms MediaTek TrustZone TEE is active. Used on MTK and some Samsung Exynos devices.
checks.remediation: Informational. Apply Mobicore/t-base TEE security patches from MediaTek. Verify no known Mobicore CVEs are unpatched.

checks.label: Samsung TEEGRIS TEE Detection
checks.description: Samsung TEEGRIS is Samsung's proprietary TrustZone OS replacing Mobicore on Exynos 9810+ devices. Provides hardware-backed security services.
checks.remediation: Informational. TEEGRIS is Samsung's TEE on newer Exynos devices. Ensure Knox/TEE patches are applied.

checks.label: Google Trusty TEE Device Node
checks.description: Google Trusty TEE IPC device node. Trusty is Google's open-source TrustZone OS used in Android reference hardware and some OEM devices.
checks.remediation: Informational. Trusty TEE presence confirms Google-managed TrustZone environment.

checks.label: Trusty TEE Properties
checks.description: Google Trusty TEE system properties. Indicates Trusty TrustZone OS is active as the TEE implementation.
checks.remediation: Informational. Verify Trusty version is up to date with Android security patches.

checks.label: Hardware Gatekeeper HAL
checks.description: Hardware Gatekeeper HAL must be present for TEE-backed password/PIN authentication. Software fallback gatekeeper is weaker.
checks.remediation: Ensure hardware-backed gatekeeper HAL is present and not falling back to software implementation.

checks.label: KASLR (Kernel Address Space Layout Randomization)
checks.description: If /proc/kallsyms returns non-zero addresses, KASLR may not be fully effective or the process has CAP_SYSLOG. Zero addresses confirm KASLR is masking kernel symbols.
checks.remediation: Ensure kernel is compiled with CONFIG_RANDOMIZE_BASE=y and restrict /proc/kallsyms to root via CONFIG_KALLSYMS_ALL=n.

checks.label: FORTIFY_SOURCE via libc
checks.description: FORTIFY_SOURCE adds compile-time buffer overflow checks to libc functions. All Android system binaries should be built with -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2.
checks.remediation: Informational. Android 4.2+ enables FORTIFY_SOURCE for system binaries by default. Verify custom binaries are also compiled with FORTIFY_SOURCE.

checks.label: Device Provisioned (Setup Wizard Complete)
checks.description: device_provisioned indicates whether initial device setup completed. A value of 0 means the device is stuck in (or has been reset into) the setup wizard, which is a partially-configured state often with weaker defaults. Critical for kiosk and POS deployments to confirm post-provisioning state.
checks.remediation: Complete the device setup flow. If the value is 0 unexpectedly, the device may have been factory reset; reprovision through the standard onboarding.

checks.label: WebView SafeBrowsing Enabled
checks.description: WebView SafeBrowsing protects in-app web content from malicious URLs (similar to Chrome SafeBrowsing). Null or empty means the per-device override is unset and WebView uses its own default (typically enabled). Explicit 0 means an admin or app has disabled it.
checks.remediation: If the value is 0, restore WebView default by clearing the setting: 'settings delete global webview_safe_browsing_state'.

checks.label: io_uring Restriction (kernel 6.6+)
checks.description: io_uring has been one of the most productive Linux kernel exploitation surfaces of recent years (a large share of kernel LPE bugs and exploit-competition wins). Android restricts it two ways: seccomp blocks it for untrusted apps, and GKI 6.6+ kernels expose the kernel.io_uring_disabled sysctl. 2 = io_uring disabled for everyone (strongest). 1 = restricted to privileged processes (Android's hardened default on kernels that ship the knob). 0 = unrestricted, which needlessly re-opens a major kernel attack surface and fails this check. NO_SYSCTL = the kernel predates the knob (5.x GKI); those builds rely on seccomp alone and are reported as acceptable rather than failing, since the sysctl simply does not exist there.
checks.remediation: If the value is 0, restore the restriction: 'echo 2 > /proc/sys/kernel/io_uring_disabled' (root), and fix whatever init/vendor script relaxed it so the setting survives reboot. Value 1 or 2 is expected stock posture on Android 15+ devices with 6.6+ kernels.

checks.label: 16KB Page Size Build
checks.command: V=$(getprop ro.product.build.16k_page.enabled 2>/dev/null); P=$(getconf PAGE_SIZE 2>/dev/null); echo "16k_build=${V:-unset} page_size=${P:-unknown}"
checks.description: Android 15+ supports 16KB memory pages (and Android 16+ requires new device support for it on arm64). Larger pages are primarily a performance feature, but they also perturb heap-grooming and page-spray assumptions baked into many public kernel and userspace exploits, so recording the page size is useful audit context when assessing exploit exposure. Reports the 16KB build property and the runtime PAGE_SIZE (4096 or 16384). Informational only: 4KB remains a fully supported, secure configuration.
checks.remediation: Nothing to fix. When refreshing fleet hardware, note that Android 16+ launch devices increasingly ship 16KB-page kernels, and in-house native code (JNI .so files) must be rebuilt with 16KB-aligned ELF segments to run on them.
